properties.description: On April 7, 2025, the City of Seattle Department of Construction & Inspections (SDCI) Code Compliance Division cited the Applicant with a Shoreline Violation (Record Number 1060659-VI) for a series of unauthorized exterior developments conducted within the steep-slope hazardous area and shoreline jurisdiction (the shoreline jurisdiction encompasses the entire subject property) associated with Elliott Bay (Puget Sound). The cited unauthorized developments included installation of a new staircase, modifications to the bulkhead and the area landward of the bulkhead, excavation at the toe of the slope, vegetation removal, and placement of cement (impervious) surfaces behind the bulkhead. However, several components of the unauthorized development are expected to be considered repair or maintenance of existing structures, as the previously existing features were no longer safe for continued use and were replaced within their original development footprints. These elements include the replacement wooden staircase along the southern western portion of the subject property and the replacement of the landscaping wall located landward of the bulkhead. Additionally, based on the geotechnical assessment provided by Migizi Group, Inc. (MGI), the completed unauthorized work has not adversely affected slope stability or contributed to slope erosion at the subject property. Accordingly, the Applicant is pursuing after-the-fact authorization through the shoreline variance permitting pathway for the completed work within the shoreline jurisdiction. The Applicant remains committed to ensuring that the overall project results in no net loss of shoreline ecological function compared to pre-project conditions and anticipates that the proposed actions will achieve a net gain in shoreline ecological function.

properties.description:
***Need DAP ASSIGNMENT for parcel number 7129302620***

Hello,

This is an application to build a "Cottage Housing Development" on an empty parcel of land (7129302620). This parcel doesn't yet have an address. I have been instructed to say "Please assign address for vacant parcel 7129302620.". 

This is a "green" project that consists of 4 separate cottages and covered parking. This parcel is in an Environmentally Critical Area (Potential landslide/steep slope). While this parcel is mostly sloped there is a portion that is actually flat. There are homes higher up on the slope and a home that is adjacent to this parcel on the slope. 

The proposed structures are cohesive with the nature of the parcel. They are underground earth-sheltered structures with green roofs/living roofs. They are simple rectangle structures that are one story studios/one bedrooms. These structures are essentially retaining walls that double as dwellings. Meaning, they will essentially be basements that are nearly completely covered with soil/grass. These structures will be anchored by "heels" and "toes". It is important to note that theses structures do not result in impervious surfaces due to their nature.

The grass "roofs" function to soak up rain, however drainage would be added to pass rainfall to a Rainwise cistern -this parcel qualifies for that program.

The introduction of this Cottage housing development will stabilize the ground for neighboring parcels and will be an overall positive additional to the area. 

Very respectfully,

Austin Payne and Kyara Tabosa

properties.description: Washington State Ferries proposes to install electrical equipment to support future operation of hybrid diesel-electric ferry vessels at the Seattle Terminal on Elliott Bay. The project includes installing the following components: electrical equipment on the uplands at Pier 48 to connect to existing Seattle City Light electrical feeders; two submarine conduits in Elliott Bay from Pier 48 uplands to the Seattle Terminal pier; new decking on the Seattle Terminal pier to support on-deck electrical equipment within new protective canopies; two in-water vessel charging system (VCS) platforms to support hybrid vessels at Seattle Terminal Slips 1 and 3; protective dolphins for the VCS platforms; and two overwater catwalks to allow maintenance access from the pier to the VCS platforms. Also included is removal of two existing floating concrete dolphins and timber debris from the seafloor. See submitted project narrative and site plan for additional details.

To remodel an existing house and add two modular buildings on site for use by Villa Comunitaria, Duwamish River Community Coalition, and Duwamish Valley Youth Corp.

The initial phase of the project will include the remodel of an existing house and addition of two modular buildings on the adjacent parcel. Site improvements at this initial phase include a parking lot with stormwater facilities and utility connections.  
The modular buildings will remain on the site for five years while the stakeholder coalition organizes fundraising. 
The subsequent phase will include the demolition of the existing house and removal of the modular buildings. This future design will be a 2-3 story multipurpose community services building, with a 3,000sf multipurpose room, and smaller parking lot.

properties.description:
I am writing to request a usage permit for dockside access behind 1800 Westlake Ave N to operate a hot tub boat rental business called Lux Hot Tub Boats (LHTB).

LHTB will be storing 4 Spacruzzi hot tub boats at Slip E20. These 295-gallon vessels use salt water chlorination systems and will require grey water disposal to the city sewer line, with water changes only as needed. The boats are equipped with ozone filtration, plus portable water filtration systems for sanitation.

The electric and propane-powered hot tubs are eco-friendly options that will limit air and lake pollution risks. All embarking and disembarking of rental guests will happen at the shoreline dock -no customers will access the moorage slips.

My business address is LHTB, 1800 Westlake Ave N, Suite 301, Seattle, WA 98109. Please let me know if any additional information is required for the usage permit application. I look forward to hearing from you.

properties.description:
The area under our waterfront deck (9ft x12ft) was backfilled with construction debris, beach sand and clay chunks. The debris included several unsightly large chunks of concrete  leaning against the support for the deck. Additionally, there is an old drainage pipe that is failing. We want to clear the debris, improve and re-connect the drainage, and add a small  wood and post wall (3ft high x12 ft wide), to hide the foundation and drainage pipes and provide storage for our kayak and SUP. There are existing concrete stairs and a large concrete chunks which we want to mortar together to make a sitting area and walkway access for SUP storage. 

The face of the seawall has some cracks, but is otherwise sound. We would like to fill the voids with concrete patch to slow the degradation of the surface. 

On the east boundary of our property, along the driveway, we want to move the east fence line 4 feet out, to the property line. This will involve removing a 4'x20' paved strip which will then be maintained as permeable landscaping. Changes to the fence line does not impact the neighbors view.  

The purpose of the moving the fence line is to secure our property, enclose our dog, provide privacy and visibly establish our ownership. This is, in part, a response to 5 years of litigation by our neighbor who attempted to adversely possess that portion of our property which was outside the original fence line. She lost in court twice, at great expense to all concerned. Her home is built within 8 feet of our mutual north-south property line. A later remodel added stairs and landing 1 foot from the property line, affording us little privacy and fueling her desire for our land. Her home has been a rental property for 5 years and is about to go on the market. We do not want to go through this again with a new neighbor. 

Thank you.

Geotechnical review has determined that shoring walls as shown can completely stabilize the site until such time as a normal building permit can be obtained.

The slide area has extensively disturbed and altered the pre-existing ECA area. We seek pre submittal review about how this affects the allowable ECA 30% disturbance tally (the slide disturbed over 35% of the ECA area). We also do not know how to apply height calculations to this situation (the slide dropped the existing elevation, which we seek to restore, along the proposed west face of the home).

The home is not part of this emergency permit relief request.m This request will supplement previous pre submittal conferences that did not cover the current situation.

properties.description:
The proposed project is to convert an existing 1 story, 5400sf mortuary building into the new home for the Rainier Valley Food Bank. 

The scope of work includes expanding and remodeling the existing building to allow food bank programs and operations to move in. Proposed spaces and alterations the design team is considering include: adding an interior or exterior walk-in cooler and a walk-in freezer; converting the existing lobby into a commercial kitchen with walk-up to-go window; adding a larger entry canopy; converting a large room into a grocery store-like distribution space; adding a small mezzanine; adding a loading dock; converting some existing parking spaces into a garden and waste enclosure; expand the building toward Rainier Ave by ~3900sf for additional office and staff support spaces.
There is also interest to activate and occupy the site with a temporary food village during the design, permitting, and construction process.

properties.description:
"The goal of this process is to build a single family house on this lot maximizing the square footage to due the very expensive costs to build (given that the entire area is a steep slope with potential landslides).  We would also like to align ourselves with Seattle's Master Design Plans to enhance the Single Family Neighborhoods by adding 2 ADUs to the project.
The ECA Variance request is here because the property has Type IV Ns wetlands less than 1000 sq ft, riparian corridor, steep slopes, and shoreline districts.  there is a stormwater culvert which runs through the middle of this steeply sloped property, noted as a non fish-bearing Riparian Corridor, and in minimizing the riparian management area to 50 feet and reducing the yards by up to 25%, I would not be able to build a house that would meet reasonable use standards for the cost to build while staying outside of the steep slope buffers and staying outside of the Shoreline District.  And given that an ECA Variance is less environmentally impactful than a Shoreline Variance, we want to stay away from modifications that would trigger a Shoreline Variance.  Instead, we will move the house and ADUs away from the Shoreline District and toward the wetlands and the steeper slopes.  Given the Wetlands are Type IV Ns < 1000 sq ft, we plan to fill those in and mitigate them elsewhere on the property.
In addition, the property should qualify for a Shoreline Exemption according the the SMC codes that I have read, thus I will by applying for this as well."

properties.description:
The King County Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) proposes to conduct maintenance repairs on the existing Denny Way combined sewer overflow (CSO) regulator. This WTD facility exists mostly on parcel number 7666202251, although the work area will extend onto the adjacent parcel 7666202250 (owned by Seattle Parks and Recreation) and Seattle right-of-way (ROW, owned by SDOT). There is no address associated with these parcels or ROW. The existing concrete pavilion overlays and protects the subterranean outfall gates of the CSO regulator and is surrounded by a protective layer of large diameter seawall rock (riprap) on the shoreline of Elliot Bay. Wave and tidal action against the riprap and pavilion have begun to erode the pavilion structure, putting the outfall gates at risk. The project therefore proposes to stabilize the plaza wall footing subgrade, repair damage in the seawall, and prevent further erosion of the shoreline around the Denny Way Regulator and Plaza. This project includes the removal of existing riprap to expose the plaza wall footings that have been undermined by tidal and wave action. The footing subgrade will be stabilized by pumping low strength concrete or flowable fill into the void spaces created by erosion of granular material from beneath the footings. Upon completion of stabilizing the plaza wall footings, the seawall will be repaired by replacing existing rock removed to repair the footings. Additional large diameter rock import will be placed to build up the shoreline revetment to protect the plaza walls and regulator transition structure.  Repair of the seawall will stabilize the shoreline, prevent further erosion around the Denny Way regulator, and restore the integrity of the surrounding plaza walls and concrete hardscape. The project will also increase the safety of staff working at the Regulator after dark and protect the Plaza's integrated artwork. 

The project construction will occur above the High Tide Line (HTL) that occurs at 10 feet NAVD88. All project work will be conducted in the dry. Temporary fencing will be erected in the surrounding upland areas to create a high-visibility barrier between the project site and the park-users. For site access a temporary construction access road and construction haul route will be established from the intersection of Broad Street and Alaskan Way along the Elliott Bay Trail. Environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and shoreline occur within or near the project area. No vegetation will be impacted by the project.

properties.description:
This building built in 1926 has a non-conforming use as a triplex in a single family zone.  This non-conforming use as a triplex is based on an electrical permit from the 1960s.  Owner wishes to update the zoning on this property to reflect current codes.  Per owner's understanding, owner believes that this property could be converted to a single family residence with two ADUs.  Owner lives in the largest unit which is considered the main residence.  The other two units, which owner wishes to convert to ADUs, were recently renovated (2010 for one unit and 2011 for the other unit) under permits.  As a result owner believes that these units should pass most if not all permit requirements in order to establish these two units as legal ADUs.  

However, currently two of the units have entrances that are street facing (the main unit and what is currently known as Unit #3). When Unit #3 was renovated in 2010, under City of Seattle permits, a new entry for Unit #3 was created within the existing building envelope.  Prior to the renovation, the building space which was to become the new entry for Unit #3 was an additional entry for the main unit.  Hence the building always had two entrances facing the street (see attached 1969 photo of house). Further, the new entrance for Unit #3 is visible as a black gate from the street.  When the gate is opened, there are stairs that lead up to Unit #3 and the main door for Unit #3, which is not visible from the street.

properties.description:
ECA Variance for lot 8124100111:

The goal of this process is to build a single family house on this lot maximizing the square footage to due the very expensive costs to build (given that the entire area is a steep slope with potential landslides).  We would also like to align ourselves with Seattle's Master Design Plans to enhance the Single Family Neighborhoods by adding 2 DADUs to the project.

The ECA Variance request is here because the property has Type IV Ns wetlands less than 1000 sq ft, riparian corridor, steep slopes, and shoreline districts.  there is a stormwater culvert which runs through the middle of this steeply sloped property, noted as a non fish-bearing Riparian Corridor, and in minimizing the riparian management area to 50 feet and reducing the yards by up to 25%, I would not be able to build a house that would meet reasonable use standards for the cost to build while staying outside of the steep slope buffers and staying outside of the Shoreline District.  And given that an ECA Variance is less environmentally impactful than a Shoreline Variance, we want to stay away from modifications that would trigger a Shoreline Variance.  Instead, we will move the house and ADUs away from the Shoreline District and toward the wetlands and the steeper slopes.  Given the Wetlands are Type IV Ns < 1000 sq ft, we plan to fill those in and mitigate them elsewhere on the property.

In addition, the property should qualify for a Shoreline Exemption according the the SMC codes that I have read, thus I will by applying for this as well.

Lastly, we are Building Green and plan to submit for Priority Green Facilitated.  We have done research here but would like assistance in navigating this process.

Thus, I would like to discuss access, stormwater, utilities, building restrictions, Built Green departures from the norms I can take advantage of during the permitting processes, and specifically tailored submittal requirements for my project.

Some infill and grading will be required in the area of the new modular block wall.  The proposed grading is seen to be very minor in scope.

This project proposes to remove the old tree stump and make in-kind repairs to the rock retaining wall in the same location.  In addition, this project proposes to replace a lower rock retaining wall at the rear, south property line area with a modular concrete block wall. 

Replacing the tree stump will require a small amount of infill and grading in the immediate area.  Drainage will be added behind the repaired wall and tied to an existing yard drainage system.  Some infill and grading will be required in the area of the new modular block wall.  The proposed grading is seen to be very minor in scope.. 5030  BEACH DR SW

properties.description: The site has two covered moorage piers with several slips on each pier.  There are also three  existing open moorage finger piers.  The piers abut the shoreline where a concrete and wood apron extends across the majority of the shoreline.  There is a single moorage float off of the eastern pier that is accessed via a wooden ramp from the eastern pier.  The proposed project is to replace the existing solid decked moorage float built on large logs with a new fully grated moorage float built on solid plastic, foam filled flotation tubs.  The existing mooring pile and access ramp to the moorage float will be retained.  The new float will be the same size, location and configuration as the existing moorage float avoiding impacts to lake bottom below.  No additional work is proposed.

properties.description:
Address is between 1101 Alaskan Way and 1201 Alaskan Way.

Piers 55 & 56 LLC proposes to remove approximately 2,200 SF of the existing Pier 55.5's east apron and with it the demolition of (38) creosote treated timber piles and (10) steel stub pile repairs. The existing timber pier will be replaced with a pier consisting of (8) 20-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles, (4) 20-inch-diameter batter steel pipe piles, and (4) 24-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles supporting cast-in-place concrete pile caps with precast concrete deck panels. Additionally (2) 10-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles will be driven with a vibratory hammer at the north and south ends of the Pier 55.5 east apron underneath Piers 56 and 55, respectively. The new concrete deck will be precast concrete panels designed to the International Building Code (IBC) occupancy requirements of 100 psf live load and to accommodate an AASHTO H10 vehicle design criteria. The center bent of the proposed new pier, approximately a sixth of the overall square footage, will also be designed to accommodate a future 150-ton crawler crane which will support the Pier's long-term development plans of maintenance and replacement of Pier 55 and other portions of Pier 55.5.

There will be a reduction in the overall number of piles used in the proposed improvements to the existing pier. The overall footprint of the proposed pier will remain the same as the existing pier; therefore, no new overwater coverage would be created. Existing timber elements have deteriorated and the structure is in need of maintenance or replacement to increase public safety and to bring the pier to current building codes, as pier does not meet current seismic design codes. In addition, a majority of the east apron of Pier 55.5 is currently closed off from all access as it has been deemed a public safety hazard due to damage from the Elliot Bay Seawall Project and construction.
